title: 「The fact that 句」
titleEn: Using the fact that to treat an established situation as a noun unit

omissions: English versions of Chinese-only Important Rules and Benefits headings are faithful editorial translations.

formula: Subject + verb + the fact that + subject + verb

formulas.formula: Subject + verb + the fact that + subject + verb
The fact that + subject + verb + singular verb + other information
Subject + verb/adjective + preposition + the fact that + subject + verb

rules.zh: that 後面必須是完整子句 that 後面通常需要有自己的主語和動詞。 這裏沒有完整表達「發生了甚麼事情」。
rules.en: That must be followed by a complete clause with its own subject and verb; otherwise the structure does not fully state what happened.
examples: The fact that the train is late annoys passengers.
Subject：the train
Verb：is

rules.zh: 整個 the fact that 子句作主語時，視為單數 不能使用： 即使 that 子句內有複數名詞，整個 the fact that... 仍被視為一項事實，因此主要動詞通常使用單 數形式。
rules.en: When the fact that-clause is the subject, treat the whole unit as singular. Even if the that-clause contains plural nouns, the entire construction represents one fact, so the main verb is normally singular.

rules.zh: 本練習必須保留 that 在部分日常 that 子句中，that 有時可以省略： 但是，在固定結構 the fact that 中，本練習必須保留 that：
rules.en: Keep that in the fact that structure for this lesson. Although that may sometimes be omitted in ordinary that-clauses, it must be retained in the fixed the fact that pattern practised here.

rules.zh: 不要把未證實的說法隨意稱為 fact 使用 the fact that 表示說話者把後面的內容視為真實或已確定。 因此，當一個說法仍然有爭議、只是一種可能性或個人觀點時，不應隨意使用 fact。 較適合的詞包括：
rules.en: Do not call an unverified claim a fact. The fact that presents the following content as true or established, so it should not be used casually for a disputed statement, mere possibility or personal view. More suitable alternatives include the idea that, the claim that, the belief that, the possibility that and the suggestion that.
examples: the idea that
the claim that
the belief that
the possibility that
the suggestion that

rules.zh: The fact that 與 The idea that 的分別 表示後面的內容被視為真實、已發生或已確定。 航班被取消是一項已發生的事情。 表示後面的內容是一個觀點、信念、概念或建議，不一定已被證實。 「金錢可以買到幸福」是一個可被討論的觀點，而不是公認事實。 Important Comparison 重要比較 這裏批評的是一個普遍觀念。 這裏描述的是一項已發生並可確認的事情。 Gold-Standard Reminder 核心提醒 不要只因為 the fact that 聽起來較正式，便用它代替 the idea that。 ● fact：真實或被視為已確定的事情 ● idea：觀點、概念或仍可被質疑的想法
rules.en: Use the fact that for content treated as true, completed or established, and the idea that for a view, belief, concept or suggestion that need not be proven. A cancelled flight is an event that happened, whereas the claim that money can buy happiness is debatable rather than an accepted fact. In the comparison, the idea that criticizes a general belief, while the fact that describes a confirmed event. Do not substitute the fact that merely because it sounds more formal: a fact is real or treated as established, while an idea is a concept or view that may still be questioned.
examples: fact：真實或被視為已確定的事情
idea：觀點、概念或仍可被質疑的想法
The fact that the flight was cancelled upset the passengers.
The idea that money can buy happiness is widely debated.
The idea that every student learns in the same way is unrealistic.
The fact that every student received the same paper is important.

benefits.zh: 清楚表明某件事被視為真實 使用 the fact that 可以告訴讀者：後面的內容不是純粹的想法，而是一項已發生或已確定的事 情。
benefits.en: It clearly presents information as real or established, telling readers that what follows is not merely an idea but something that has happened or been determined.
examples: The fact that the road is closed means we must turn back.

benefits.zh: 把完整情況變成一個名詞單位 你可以把一整件事情放在主語、受詞或介詞後。 在這句中，整個 the fact that she apologised 都是主語。
benefits.en: It turns a complete situation into one noun unit that can appear as a subject, object or after a preposition; in the example, the entire phrase the fact that she apologised functions as the subject.
examples: The fact that she apologised surprised me.

benefits.zh: 連接一項事實與人們的反應或判斷 這個句型特別適合表達： ● 某件事令人驚訝； ● 某件事令人擔心； ● 某件事不能被忽略； ● 某件事造成某種結果。
benefits.en: It connects a fact with a reaction or judgement and is especially useful for saying that something is surprising, worrying, impossible to ignore or responsible for a particular result.
examples: The fact that nobody checked the door worried the manager.

benefits.zh: 把兩個相關句子合併起來 不用分開寫兩句，你可以直接把事實與結果連接起來。 第二個版本更清楚地展示兩項資料之間的關係。
benefits.en: It combines two related sentences by joining a fact directly to its result; the combined version displays the relationship between the two pieces of information more clearly.
examples: The fact that the bus is often late annoys passengers.

benefits.zh: 適合用於解釋、報告及討論 這個句型可以配合以下常用表達： 掌握這些組合後，你可以更有條理地分析問題、解釋情況或表達判斷。
benefits.en: It is useful in explanations, reports and discussions. Common combinations include accept, recognise or ignore the fact that; be aware of the fact that; despite the fact that; and draw attention to the fact that. Mastering them helps you analyse issues, explain situations and express judgements systematically.
examples: accept the fact that
recognise the fact that
ignore the fact that
be aware of the fact that
despite the fact that
draw attention to the fact that
